newsitem.title: INDIA: India SBI ties up with GE Capital.
newsitem.headline: India SBI ties up with GE Capital.

text.p: India's biggest commercial bank, State Bank of India (SBI) said on Saturday it signed an agreement with GE Capital Services, a unit of U.S.-based General Electric to set up a credit card joint venture.

"Through this agreement GE Capital ... will provide SBI with appropriate technology, products and processing capability that will enable us develop payment card business," SBI chairman P.G. Kakodkar told reporters.
State-run SBI has more than 8,900 branches in India and abroad.
"Our target will be to have at least two million cards ... at the end of three years of operation," Kakodkar said.
SBI Credit Cards Ltd will have a capital of one billion rupees, and the holdings of both partners will be worked out in a month's time, he said.
